text:
Alex: Heads-up: Q2 contract planning — we need to pick reserved GPU tiers for 3 enterprise customers. Looking for input on tradeoffs: price vs headroom.
Mira: Can we reuse the table from last quarter? numbers changed after the APAC region rollout.
Sam: linking dataset: https://internal.redwood/metrics/pool-usage/quarterly — includes tokens/s, reqs/s, and 95th pct usage per pool.
Jordan: Short version: customer A needs ~200 reqs/min at p95 latency 300ms on hosted. Translating to throughput from logs: ~42k tokens/s during peak -> roughly 3.5 A100-equivalent GPUs if we assume perfect packing. But batching variance and cold KV-cache means add ~25% buffer.
Alex: So roughly 5 GPUs reserved for Customer A? note: 12mo commit saves ~30% vs on-demand but locks capacity.
Priya (Finance): FYI finance threshold is utilization >= 60% on reserved to justify the commit. We can handle a 3-month ramp period in accounting.
Mira: Ops question: can Dedicated autoscale burst to hosted/global pool if reserved pool saturated? Need fallback policy spelled out for SLA.
Jordan: Yes, smart routing can fail over to hosted but you pay higher per-token cost and regional latency may increase. Must ensure network egress limits in the target region aren't hit.
Sam: Quick calc attached here for visibility:
```
peak_tokens_s = 42000
gpu_tokens_s_per_A100 = 12000
gpus_raw = ceil(42000 / 12000) = 4
buffer = 1.25 -> target_gpus = 5
```
Alex: If we sign 5 GPUs for 12 months cost = $X/mo (back-of-envelope) — question: do we split this commit per-customer or host as a shared pool? Customer A wants 80% SLA isolation.
Priya (Finance): Splitting increases billing complexity but gives clearer chargeback. Alternative: 3 guaranteed GPUs + 2 shared GPUs for burst. That raises utilization and reduces wasted spend.
Mira: That pattern helps utilization but we need to simulate tail-latency when shared GPUs are full. Also confirm network/firewall changes for cross-customer routing.
OpsBot: Created alert INC-5123 reserved-pool-plan-draft and assigned to Sam, Jordan.
Jordan: Note: check AZ capacity in eu-west-1 — we hit instance-type shortage last month, which delayed replenishment. If shortages persist, reserved capacity provisioning could be delayed by weeks. Need a contingency (different AZ or region).
Sam: Action: I'll run a Monte Carlo sim on arrival variance + batching efficiency and post a sensitivity matrix by EOD. Will include percentiles for tokens/s, reqs/s, and resulting GPU count for 10/25/50/75/95 pct.
Alex: Also add a cost sensitivity for 0/10/25/50% utilization scenarios and break-even vs on-demand.
Priya (Finance): I will model cashflow and break-even horizon for 6/12/24 month commits and share updated numbers.
Mira: Thanks — once sims and finance numbers are in I'll schedule a 30m sync with Sales & Solutions.
Jordan: One more product note: consider offering a short-term trial credit to customers to reduce ramp risk and protect utilization targets.
Sam: ack, will include trial credit effects in the sim.
Alex: Thanks all :thumbsup:
